title: “‘You Can See Everything’ Tops Monday Box Office, Aims to Unseat ‘Clayface’”
body:
The modest‑budget documentary *You Can See Everything* topped Monday’s domestic box‑office, pulling in roughly $2.5 million and nudging the long‑running superhero thriller *Clayface* toward the bottom of the weekend’s rankings. The surprise win marks the first time in three weeks that a non‑franchise film has displaced the comic‑book entry from the top spot, and it underscores a growing appetite for off‑beat, character‑driven fare among moviegoers still emerging from a pandemic‑induced slump.

Directed by the enigmatic duo of Nathan Fielder and Elizabeth Holmes, *You Can See Everything* is a hybrid of investigative documentary and surreal comedy that follows a group of Gen‑Z activists as they attempt to expose the hidden surveillance infrastructure of major tech firms. The film’s low‑key marketing campaign relied heavily on viral TikTok clips and word‑of‑mouth buzz, a strategy that appears to have paid off. While its opening weekend earnings of $2.5 million are modest compared to blockbuster standards, the per‑theater average of $12,400 signals a strong turnout in limited‑release venues across major cities such as New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago.

Industry analysts point to several factors behind the film’s unexpected surge. First, *You Can See Everything* arrived at a moment when audiences are increasingly fatigued by the endless parade of superhero sequels and franchise spin‑offs. The film’s fresh aesthetic—shot in a gritty, handheld style and peppered with candid interviews—offers a stark contrast to the polished CGI spectacles that dominate the summer slate. Second, the involvement of Nathan Fielder, known for his off‑beat humor on television, brings a built‑in fan base that is eager to see his transition to the big screen. Finally, the controversial presence of Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced Theranos founder, adds a layer of intrigue that has sparked debate on social media platforms, driving curious viewers to the theater.

The box‑office dip for *Clayface* is unlikely to be permanent, but the shift highlights a broader trend: studios are now forced to reckon with a more discerning audience that values originality alongside spectacle. *Clayface*, which opened to $15.6 million and has held the No. 2 spot for three consecutive weeks, has seen its weekly gross fall by nearly 30 percent since its debut, suggesting that even a well‑executed superhero film can lose steam when faced with compelling alternatives. Executives at major studios are reportedly reassessing release windows, considering whether to pair smaller, high‑concept titles with tentpole releases or to give them standalone breathing room.

Critics have responded favorably to *You Can See Everything*, praising its daring blend of satire and genuine investigative journalism. Review aggregator scores hover in the high 80s, with particular commendation for the film’s ability to humanize complex data‑privacy issues without sacrificing entertainment value. The documentary’s success may also signal a resurgence of the “documentary‑drama” hybrid, a format that thrived in the early 2020s with titles like *The Social Dilemma* and *Won’t You Be My Neighbor?*. If the trend continues, studios might allocate more resources to similar projects, potentially reshaping the mid‑budget market segment.

Looking ahead, the coming weeks will test whether *You Can See Everything* can sustain its momentum beyond the initial curiosity spike. Its second‑week projections suggest a drop of 45 percent, a typical pattern for limited releases, but strong word‑of‑mouth could keep it in the top ten for an extended run. Meanwhile, *Clayface* is slated to expand into additional international markets, where it may recoup some of the domestic slowdown. Regardless of the outcome, the Monday box‑office upset serves as a reminder that innovative storytelling can still capture audience attention in an era dominated by franchise juggernauts, and that the next big cinematic surprise may come from the most unexpected corners of the industry.
